response.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.country, cs.wins - COALESCE(LAG(cs.wins) OVER (PARTITION BY cs.constructorId, r.year ORDER BY r.round), 0) AS gain FROM constructorStandings cs JOIN races r ON r.raceId = cs.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId), ca AS (SELECT country, AVG(gain) AS avg_gain FROM s GROUP BY country), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gain) AS m FROM ca), k AS (SELECT ca.country, ca.avg_gain, ca.avg_gain - m1.m AS ex1 FROM ca, m1 WHERE ca.avg_gain > m1.m), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gain) AS m FROM k), f AS (SELECT k.avg_gain, k.ex1, k.avg_gain - m2.m AS ex2 FROM k, m2 WHERE k.avg_gain > m2.m) SELECT AVG(avg_gain) AS mean_avg_wins, AVG(ex1) AS mean_excess_over_all_mean, AVG(ex2) AS mean_excess_over_group_mean FROM f

assumptions.assumption: The previous round is the constructor's previous standings row in the same season, ordered by races.round. If a constructor skipped a round, its earlier row is still used. The first row in a season is compared against 0.
Each country's average is taken over its standings rows. The mean of all country averages is unweighted, so each country counts once.
Both thresholds are strict (>). The second mean is the mean of the first-stage kept countries' averages.
